A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of A Simple Model of Inference Scaling Laws. Their text, equations, seven figures, references, and Appendix A support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original Fashion-MNIST VAE experiments, including reconstruction coverage and trial-error correlations in Figures 5–6. Appendix A provides experimental details and reconstruction examples.

after.justification: v2 retains the original VAE reconstruction experiments and their outcomes in Section 4 and Appendix A, including Figures 5–7.

M1.justification: The memorization model, Beta-distributed failure probabilities, effective-trial construction, and VAE remain unchanged. Calling epsilon an error instead of an error distribution beside Eq. (2) clarifies wording without changing the model.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Fashion-MNIST reconstruction task and the same LLM MATH curves attributed to Brown et al. (2024). No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Figure 1 retains Pythia-2.8B, Llama-3-8B, and Gemma-2B and the same analytical comparisons. The VAE comparisons also remain unchanged. The added related-work citations do not introduce evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A retain the same settings, including the first 400 Fashion-MNIST samples, 1000 training epochs, temperature T = 1.1, reconstruction-error metric, thresholds, and pass@k procedure.

E4.justification: Figures 5–7 retain the same threshold comparisons, reconstruction-error distributions, trial-correlation and eigenvalue analyses, and reconstruction examples. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, independent training-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The repeated inference-trial analyses and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: The fitted parameters, curves, and findings in Figures 1–3 and the VAE results and examples in Figures 5–7 are unchanged. The pages containing these results are visually identical.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(15), formal assumptions, and derivations are retained. The wording adjustment concerning epsilon beside Eq. (2) does not alter the mathematical model or subsequent reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: two explanations of inference scaling, power-law inference loss, its connection to compute, and controlled VAE validation.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 removes the suggestion that errors accumulate because of the learned internal probability distribution and sampling temperature. This deletes one tentative mechanism explanation; the later interpretations and limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A is identical, retaining the VAE architecture, temperature, training subset, loss, optimizer, learning rate, and epoch count. No implementation details or code/data-access information are added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Levi and Oz (2023, 2024) and Nam et al. (2024), alongside a brief connection to random matrix theory and underlying data properties. The paper's positioning around inference scaling remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Sections 2–3 receive limited wording and grammar edits, an explicit Hutter citation, clarification of epsilon, and deletion of one explanatory sentence. The displayed date is removed; section order and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Removing the title-page date and expanding text and references causes limited reflow on pages 1–3 and 11. All seven figures, their captions and plotting elements, and the appendix layout remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly updates research context and wording while retaining the same theory, claims, experimental evidence, and reproducibility information. Removing one speculative mechanism sentence has limited impact. These edits do not meaningfully strengthen or weaken the paper's overall quality.
